edition.locus: Against Marcion 4.41 (Judas’s woe; Creator’s zeal; Son of Man confession)

source_text: Vae, ait, per quem traditur filius hominis. ergo iam \'uae* constat imprecationis et comminationis inclamationem intellegendam et irato et offenso deputandam, nisi si ludas impune erat tantum sceleris relaturus. at si impune, uacat \'uae\'; si non impune, utique ab eo puniendus, in quem scelus traditionis admisit. porro si sciens passus est hominem, quem ipse comitatui suo adsciuerat, in tantum scelus ruere, noli iam de creatore circa Adam retractare quae in tuum quoque deum retorquentur: aut ignorasse illum, qui non ex prouidentia obstitit peccaturo, aut obsistere non potuisse, si (non) ignorabat, aut noluisse, si et sciebat et poterat, atque ita malitiosum iudicandum, qui passus sit hominem suum ex delicto perire. suadeo igitur agnoscas potius et in isto creatorem quam parem illi deum optimum aduersus sententiam tuam facias. nam et Petrum praesumptorie aliquid elocutum negationi potius destinando zeloten deum tibi ostendit. debuit etiam osculo tradi, propheticus scilicet Christus, ut eius scilicet filius, qui labiis a populo diligebatur. Perductus in consessum, an ipse esset Christus, interrogatur. de quo Christo Iudaei quaesissent nisi de suo? cur ergo non uel tunc alium eis prodidit? \'ut pati posset\', inquis, id est, ut ille optimus ignorantes adhuc in scelus mergeret. atquin et si dixisset, passurus esset. si dixero enim, inquit, uobis, non credetis. porro non credituri perseuerassent in necem eius. et cur non magis passurus esset, si alterius dei ac per hoc aduersarium creatoris (se) manifestasset? ergo non, ut pateretur, alium se tunc quoque supersedit ostendere, sed quoniam ex ore eius confessionem extorquere cupiebant, nec confesso tamen credituri, qui eum ex operibus scripturas adimplentibus agnouisse debuerant. ita eius fuit occultasse se, cui ultro debebatur agnitio. et tamen adhuc eis manum porrigens: abhinc, inquit, erit filius hominis sedens ad dexteram uirtutis dei. suggerebat enim se esse (de) Danihelis prophetia (filium hominis* et de psalmo Dauid (sedentem ad dexteram dei\'. itaque ex isto dicto et scripturae comparatione inluminati, quem se uellet intellegi: ergo, inquiunt, tu dei filius es? cuius dei, nisi quem solum nouerant? cuius dei, nisi quem in psalmo meminerant dixisse filio suo: sede ad dexteram meam? <sed respondit: uos dicitis, quasi: non ego\\ atquin confirmauit id se esse, quod illi dixerant, dum rursus interrogant. unde autem probabis interrogatiuo et non (et) ipsos confirmatiuo pronuntiasse: ergo tu filius dei es, ut, quia oblique ostenderat se per scripturas filium dei intellegendum, sic senserint: \'ergo tu dei es filius\', quod te non uis aperte dicere? atque ita et ille (uos dicitis\' confirmatiue respondit, et adeo sic fuit pronuntiatio eius, ut perseuerauerint in eo, quod pronuntiatio sapiebat.
pass_a_gloss: Vae = imprecatio. Iudas a prodito puniendus. Filius hominis / dextera = Creatoris Christus.
pass_b_english: ‘Woe,’ he says, ‘through whom the Son of Man is betrayed.’ Therefore already that ‘woe’ stands to be understood as an outcry of imprecation and threat and to be assigned to one angry and offended—unless Judas was going to carry such a crime with impunity. But if with impunity, the ‘woe’ is empty; if not with impunity, then he is surely to be punished by the one against whom he committed the crime of betrayal. Further, if knowingly he allowed a man whom he himself had enrolled in his company to rush into such a crime, do not now reopen against the Creator concerning Adam what is also turned back on your god: either that he was ignorant who did not from providence block the one about to sin, or that he could not block if he was not ignorant, or that he was unwilling if he both knew and could—and so is to be judged malicious, who allowed his human to perish from a delict.

I therefore urge you rather to acknowledge the Creator also in this than to make against your own sentence a ‘best’ god equal to him. For by destining Peter, who spoke something presumptuously, rather to denial, he also shows you a zealous God. He also ought to be betrayed by a kiss—prophetic Christ of course, so that he would be the son of him who was loved with lips by the people. Led into the assembly, he is asked whether he himself is the Christ. About what Christ would the Jews have asked if not about their own? Why then did he not even then produce another to them? ‘So that he could suffer,’ you say—that is, so that that ‘best’ one might plunge those still ignorant into crime. Yet even if he had said it, he would have been going to suffer. For if I tell you, he says, you will not believe. Further, those not going to believe would have persevered in his killing. And why would he not all the more have been going to suffer if he had manifested himself as of another god and thereby the Creator’s adversary?

Therefore it was not so that he might suffer that he then also forbore to show himself another, but because they desired to wring a confession from his mouth, and yet even if he confessed they would not believe—who ought to have recognized him from works fulfilling the scriptures. So it belonged to him to have hidden himself, to whom recognition was owed of its own accord. And yet still stretching a hand to them: From now on, he says, the Son of Man will be sitting at the right hand of the power of God. For he was suggesting that he was from Daniel’s prophecy the Son of Man and from David’s psalm the one sitting at God’s right hand. And so enlightened from that saying and the scripture comparison as to whom he wanted to be understood: Therefore, they say, are you God’s Son? Of whose God, if not the one alone they knew? Of whose God, if not the one whom they remembered in the psalm saying to his Son: Sit at my right hand?

But he answered: You say so—as if: not I? Yet he confirmed that he is what they had said, while they ask again. But how will you prove they pronounced interrogatively and not themselves confirmatively: Therefore you are God’s Son—so that, because he had obliquely shown through the scriptures that he was to be understood as God’s Son, they sensed: ‘Therefore you are God’s Son,’ which you do not want to say openly? And so he too answered confirmatively ‘You say,’ and so was his pronunciation that they persevered in what the pronunciation meant.

lemmas.form: ab eo puniendus, in quem scelus

lemmas.gloss: zealous God shown in Peter’s denial destiny
Son of Man at God’s right hand

choices.choice: own Creator judgment in the Judas-woe rather than invent a non-punishing best god
rejected: empty the woe into impunity to spare Marcion’s deity anger

choices.choice: read the right-hand confession as Creator’s Daniel/Psalm Christ
rejected: treat the council question as about another unknown god’s Christ

notes: Reward-and-judgment: woe/punishment; zealous Creator; Son of Man confession.
